comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs (GS) and Citigroup (C) disclose the disposal or sale of consumer lending assets, specifically involving credit cards. GS reports $14.32 billion in consumer credit card lines held for sale in connection with the planned sale of its GM co-branded portfolio, while C explicitly reports the sale of approximately $335 million of consumer loans in 2024 and notes the acquisition of a $700 million credit card portfolio. Both disclosures highlight active management of consumer loan portfolios through sales and restructuring activities.

sentences.text: • Credit card lines issued by the firm to consumers were $78.10 billion as of December 2024 and $70.82 billion as of December 2023. Such credit card lines included $14.32 billion as of December 2024 and $14.35 billion as of December 2023 of commitments classified as held for sale in connection with the planned sale of the GM co-branded credit card portfolio. These credit card lines are cancellable by the firm.
During the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, the Company sold and/or reclassified to held-for-sale (HFS) approximately $335 million and $2,166 million of consumer loans, respectively.

Except for the acquisition of an approximate $700 million credit card portfolio during the year ended December 31, 2024, the Company did not have significant purchases of consumer loans classified as held-for-investment during the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023.
